title: Rewind a failing test to hunt down a software bug
summary: Antithesis let Claude use its rewind tool to replay a failing test and probe a bug in HashiCorp software; the company shows a replay but reports no final fix.
agent_role: Claude returns to the failing execution, branches time to run diagnostic commands, works on a fix and reruns it in Antithesis. Humans write the tests and review the result.
outcome: Antithesis shows a replay of Claude investigating a bug it found in HashiCorp's Raft implementation. The post does not report the final fix.
what_they_did: Antithesis, a software testing company, let agents use its tool that can replay and rewind a test run exactly. In their demo, Claude takes a bug Antithesis found in HashiCorp's Raft, software that keeps servers in agreement. It rewinds to just before the failure and tries ideas in separate copies of the run. Then it reruns the changed code to check the fix.
how_it_went: The company shows a replay of Claude hunting the bug. They say a person no longer needs to run the tool and pass findings to the agent. No fix results are given.
worth_knowing: You need an Antithesis account (Release 64) and existing Antithesis tests that are already failing. It is a paid product, and the post is its launch announcement.
prompt: Using the antithesis-debug skill, take the failing property [property name] from Antithesis run [run ID]. Rewind to just before the assertion failed. Run diagnostic commands in branched timelines to find the root cause, and explain the sequence of events. Propose a fix and show me the diff before committing. Then launch a new Antithesis run to check that the fix holds.

curation.rationale: Mostly a vendor launch post, but it includes a concrete demo of Claude using deterministic replay to investigate a real bug in HashiCorp's Raft implementation. The outcome of the fix is not detailed.
